briefdescription.para: Scan (or rescan) a directory with snapshot or write ahead logs.

detaileddescription.para: Scan or re-scan a directory and update directory index with all log files (or snapshots) in the directory.

Read all files matching a pattern from the directory - the filename pattern is +.xlog The name of the file is based on its vclock signature, which is the sum of all elements in the vector clock recorded when the file was created. Elements in the vector reflect log sequence numbers of replicas in the asynchronous replication set (see also _cluster system space and vclock.h comments).

dir
- directory to scan
is_dir_required
- flag set if the directory should exist
: 0 - on success or flag 'is_dir_required' was set to False in xdir_scan() arguments and opendir() failed with errno ENOENT; -1 - if opendir() failed, with other than ENOENT errno either when 'is_dir_required' was set to True in xdir_scan() arguments. This function tries to avoid re-reading a file if it is already in the set of files "known" to the log dir object. This is done to speed up local hot standby and recovery_follow_local(), which periodically rescan the directory to discover newly created logs.
On error, this function throws an exception. If dir->force_recovery is true, some errors are not propagated up but only logged in the error log file.

The list of errors ignored in force_recovery = true mode includes:
a file can not be opened
some of the files have incorrect metadata (such files are skipped)
The goal of force_recovery = true mode is partial recovery from a damaged/incorrect data directory. It doesn't silence conditions such as out of memory or lack of OS resources.
